The '''2024 Fareham Borough Council election''' was held on Thursday 2 May 2024, alongside the [[2024 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections in the United Kingdom]]. All 32 members of [[Fareham Borough Council]] in [[Hampshire]] were elected following boundary changes.

The council remained under [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] majority control.

==Background==
Since its creation in 1974, only the Conservatives have ever formed majorities on the council. The party has held majorities on the council for its entire history, except between [[1986 Fareham Borough Council election|1986]] and [[1987 Fareham Borough Council election|1987]], and between [[1994 Fareham Borough Council election|1994]] and [[1999 Fareham Borough Council election|1999]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Fareham Borough Council Election Results 1973-2012 |url=https://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Fareham-1973-2012.pdf |website=Elections Centre |access-date=11 March 2024}}</ref> The [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] briefly overtook the Conservatives as the largest party in this second period of [[no overall control]], but never formed a majority.

In the [[2022 Fareham Borough Council election|previous election in 2022]], the Conservatives gained 2 seats with 45.7% of the vote, the Liberal Democrats maintained their 5 seats with 25.7%, and [[independent politician|independents]] won 1 with 3.9%. The leader of the council prior to the election was Conservative councillor Seán Woodward, who had held the post since 1999. He did not stand for re-election in 2024. After the election, the Conservatives chose Simon Martin to be their new group leader; he was formally appointed as the new leader of the council at the subsequent annual council meeting on 16 May 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Needs |first1=Noni |title=New Fareham Borough Council leader confirmed |url=https://www.dailyecho.co.uk/news/24330377.new-fareham-borough-council-leader-confirmed/ |access-date=5 July 2024 |work=Daily Echo |date=20 May 2024}}</ref>

==Boundary changes==
Fareham usually elects its councillors in halves, on a 4-year cycle. However, following boundary changes, all councillors will be elected to the new wards.<ref>{{Cite legislation UK |type=si |year=2023 |number=796 |si= The Fareham (Electoral Changes) Order 2023 |accessdate=11 March 2024 }}</ref> The change increases the number of councillors by 1.

* September 2022: Jean Kelly (Liberal Democrats) resigns; by-election held October 2022<ref>{{cite news |last1=Paine |first1=Toby |title=Fareham councillor Jean Kelly quits after moving to Liverpool - sparking political row between Liberal Democrats and Conservatives |url=https://www.portsmouth.co.uk/news/people/fareham-councillor-jean-kelly-quits-after-moving-to-liverpool-sparking-political-row-between-liberal-democrats-and-conservatives-3830036 |access-date=11 March 2024 |work=The News |date=2 September 2022}}</ref>
* October 2022: Harry Davis (Conservative) gains by-election from Liberal Democrats<ref>{{cite web |title=Local Elections Archive Project — Portchester East Ward |url=https://www.andrewteale.me.uk/leap/ward/4184/#2022-10-20 |website=www.andrewteale.me.uk |access-date=11 March 2024}}</ref>
